correctness.rationale: For the regular heptagon, chord normals reduce to 14 candidate rays; the enclosing supports have alternating heights 1 and cos(pi/7). Any optimum tightens to four selected supporting lines. Bounded choices have four integer angular gaps between 1 and 6 summing to 14. The shoelace/support-length identity gives their area. The standalone exact-rational script heptagon_cert.py verifies all 511 bounded four-normal choices, their consecutive-vertex feasibility, 14 exact algebraic zeros, and strict scaled-area gaps against the seven congruent winners; its cubic root bracket is rationally certified. The winners use edge supports with gaps 2,4,4,4, yielding the exact area and ratio in RESULT.md. Exhaustive finite enumeration is mathematically exhaustive here, not random experimentation. Independent audit not performed.

originality.rationale: Vígh (arXiv:2610.08168v1), sections 2 and 5, gives the chord-quadrilateral definition, general finite candidate method, and a numerical 1.2588... at the affine-regular heptagon, but no exact closed expression, exhaustive optimality certificate for this heptagon, or classification of its seven minimizing supporting configurations. The present result is limited to these exact and rigid details. Fodor--Grundbacher establish a universal unrestricted upper bound, not a heptagon-specific exact evaluation. A published result on minimum enclosing parallelograms of regular polygons treats a strictly smaller class of containing quadrilaterals; neither its value nor the polytope-specific quadrilateral exact bound is the present conclusion. Exact finite certificate independently proves the unreported case. Historical priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The recently proposed chord conjecture singles out finite chord-support configurations as a promising strengthening of the Kuperberg problem. The canonical regular heptagon appears as a numerically observed local extremum, but its exact algebraic ratio and optimizing directions were not established in the motivating text. The exact expression and full sevenfold equality classification provide a natural benchmark and rigid configuration in the first non-pentagonal odd example of this active approximation problem, beyond merely reporting a new decimal or running generic numerical optimization. The result does not purport to solve the global conjecture.
